sections.h2: When is property tax due in Allen County, Ohio?
sections.html:
Allen County real estate tax is paid in two installments, normally due on the second Wednesday of February and the second Wednesday of July. The county treasurer's page lists the 2026 tax year, payable in 2027, as February 10 and July 14, 2027. Bills usually go out in January and June, though the treasurer's FAQ explains that the exact date moves with whenever the auditor delivers the calculated tax file.

A seller with sewer service should ask the closing agent to check the sewer balance along with the property tax, since both flow through the treasurer's office.

sections.h2: What happens if an Allen County tax payment is late?
sections.html:
A payment postmarked within 10 days after the due date carries a 5 percent penalty, and one postmarked later carries 10 percent. The treasurer's FAQ describes these as penalties required by state law. An owner can mail in an Application for Remission to ask for a waiver.

The treasurer also posts a warning about the mail. A postmark usually shows the day the Postal Service machinery first processed the envelope, which can be a day or more after drop-off. Because Ohio law reads the postmark date, a check mailed close to the deadline can arrive late on paper. The office suggests mailing early, asking the post office for a hand-stamped postmark, or paying in person, by card or by e-check.

sections.h2: How can you pay the Allen County treasurer?
sections.html:
The office takes cash, checks, cards and e-checks, and it is closed on federal holidays. The treasurer's counter is at 237 N Main St, Suite 123, Lima, OH 45801, and the office phone is (419) 223-8515. The treasurer's home page shows a weekday close of 4:30 p.m. while its FAQ says 4:15 p.m., so call before a deadline-day trip.

  • Online through the Search and Pay Property Taxes tab, or by phone at 1-419-765-6401.
  • In person, or at the drop box by the automatic doors outside the courthouse.
  • At Superior Credit Union or The Union Bank Company branches in the county, free of charge and open to non-customers, but only from mid-January to the February deadline and from mid-June to the July deadline.
  • By card or e-check through a third-party vendor, which adds a convenience fee: 2.40 percent (with a $2 minimum) for cards and a flat $1 for e-checks.

Two payment plans exist for owners who prefer smaller bites. The TEPP in-house escrow spreads annual taxes over 10 months, and the AUTO-Pay program pulls the exact amount from a bank account on each due date or once a year on the second Wednesday in February.

sections.h2: How is an Allen County tax bill figured?
sections.html:
The treasurer's FAQ states the method plainly: market value is multiplied by 35 percent to reach assessed value, and assessed value is multiplied by the effective tax rate for the owner's political subdivision to get gross tax. Levies take effect in the year voters approve them, but the bill for that year is payable the next year. A five-year levy approved in November of one year, for instance, shows up on the bills due the following year.

The county auditor's site has a property search and a tax calculator, and the treasurer's resources section lists tax rates, tax duplicates, school districts, cities and villages, and townships. Look up your parcel there to see your own rate, because the rate depends on the school district and village or township lines.

sections.h2: How do you challenge an Allen County valuation?
sections.html:
File a Complaint Against Valuation with the county auditor between January 1 and March 31, according to the auditor's FAQ. Ohio Revised Code 5715.19 sets the deadline as March 31 of the following year or the close of first-half collection, whichever is later, and it treats a mailed complaint's postal postmark as the filing date. A private meter postmark does not count.

  • The auditor hands every complaint to the county board of revision.
  • Other parties can file a counter-complaint within 30 days of notice.
  • The board must decide an original complaint within 180 days after the last filing date.
  • While a complaint is pending, the treasurer accepts tax computed on the value you claim.
  • You must give the board all evidence you hold, or you can be barred from using it on appeal.

Destroyed or damaged property has a separate form, the Application for Valuation Deduction. The auditor says to file as soon as possible because refunds for prior years are not issued.

sections.h2: Which tax reductions can an Allen County homeowner claim?
sections.html:
The auditor's FAQ names three programs. The Owner Occupancy Credit, a 2.5 percent rollback, applies to a primary residence. The Homestead reduction covers owners who are 65 or older or who are permanently and totally disabled, and the application goes to the auditor, with postmarks accepted. CAUV lowers valuation for commercial farmland.

These credits matter when you sell, because the buyer's statement of value under section 319.202 asks whether the seller's taxes were reduced. Ask the auditor for the credits currently attached to your parcel.

sections.h2: Who owes the tax when an Allen County house sells?
sections.html:
The auditor's FAQ says taxes follow ownership and are usually prorated at closing, and that the auditor does not prorate. If closing skips the step, the new owner is the one billed. Taxes are charged on the property as it stood on January 1, so a parcel split mid-year is billed whole until someone requests a tax split. After a transfer it takes a year for the previous owner's name to clear from the treasurer's system, which does not change who must pay.

At transfer, the auditor's FAQ quotes a conveyance fee of $3.00 per thousand of the purchase price and a $.50 per parcel transfer charge. A title company will normally add both to the settlement statement.

sections.h2: What does the Allen County economy mean for housing?
sections.html:
Allen County has about 100,881 residents, and in 2020 to 2024 the Census Bureau put median household income at $64,038 and median gross rent at $922. Owners with a mortgage report median monthly costs of $1,240, and those without one $535. Workers commute 18.7 minutes on average, and 60.7 percent of residents 16 or older are in the labor force. The county counted 2,239 employer establishments and 44,251 jobs in 2023, plus retail sales of $20,786 per resident in 2022.

Those QuickFacts describe the county as a whole. The auditor's property search is the place to see what your own street's neighbors are assessed at.

faqs.q: When is the second half of property tax due in Allen County?
faqs.a: The posted due date for the 2026 tax year is Wednesday, July 14, 2027, and the first half is due Wednesday, February 10, 2027. In general both fall on the second Wednesday of their month.

faqs.q: What is the penalty for paying Allen County property tax late?
faqs.a: It is 5 percent if the payment is postmarked within 10 days after the due date and 10 percent after that. The treasurer's FAQ also offers a remission application to request a waiver.

faqs.q: Can I pay Allen County property tax with a credit card?
faqs.a: Yes. Cards and e-checks are taken online, by phone at 1-419-765-6401 and in the office, with the vendor's fee of 2.40 percent (at least $2) for cards or $1 for an e-check.

faqs.q: How do I appeal my Allen County property value?
faqs.a: File a Complaint Against Valuation with the Allen County Auditor between January 1 and March 31. The auditor then presents it to the county board of revision.

faqs.q: Who pays the property tax when I sell my Allen County home?
faqs.a: Taxes follow ownership and are usually prorated at closing. The auditor's office does not prorate them, so ask your closing agent to settle the split on the statement.
